text:
In this exercise, we will consider the span of some sets of two- and three-dimensional vectors.

Consider the vectors $$ \vvec_1 = \twovec{1}{-2}, \vvec_2 = \twovec{4}{3} $$ .

Is $\bvec = \twovec{2}{1}$ in $\laspan{\vvec_1,\vvec_2}$?

Give a geometric description of $\laspan{\vvec_1,\vvec_2}$.

Consider the vectors $$ \vvec_1=\threevec{2}{1}{3}, \vvec_2=\threevec{-2}{0}{2}, \vvec_3=\threevec{6}{1}{-1} $$ .

Is the vector $\bvec=\threevec{-10}{-1}{5}$ in $\laspan{\vvec_1,\vvec_2,\vvec_3}$?

Is the vector $\vvec_3$ in $\laspan{\vvec_1,\vvec_2,\vvec_3}$?

Is the vector $\bvec=\threevec{3}{3}{-1}$ in $\laspan{\vvec_1,\vvec_2,\vvec_3}$?

Give a geometric description of $\laspan{\vvec_1,\vvec_2,\vvec_3}$.
